Neutron governance exploit drains ≈$9.4M, forces 24-hour Cosmos Hub chain halt
–
Link
An attacker flash-bought about $20K in NTRN voting power and used it to seize control of roughly $9.4M in contract assets, gaining admin rights over the Astroport and Drop Money contracts before draining funds. Around $1.96M had already been bridged out when Cosmos Hub validators coordinated a ≈24-hour, 48-minute halt to intercept and redirect about 1.23M ATOM back to victims.
Cheap voting power controlling far larger treasury value is a structural flaw here, and it may push other Cosmos SDK chains to rethink their admin-migration permissions.

RWA perp market reaches $117B monthly volume
Trading in perpetual contracts linked to real-world assets is growing quickly, with more activity moving onchain.
In August, RWA perp trading volume reached $117.3B, up 44x year-over-year. Onchain platforms accounted for 86% of the volume, around $101B.
Equities are now the largest category at 48% of volume, followed by commodities at 28% and indices at 18%.
Open interest also grew nearly 30x, from $161M in July 2025 to $4.8B in August 2026.
The market is still small compared with traditional derivatives, but the growth shows rising demand for trading traditional assets onchain.
